title: Slices With Exactly K Odd Values
statement:
You get an array nums of positive integers and a number k. Count the contiguous slices of nums that contain exactly k odd numbers.

Slices are counted by position: two slices with the same values at different positions both count.

examples.why: A slice must contain both the 3 and the 5. It can start at index 0 or 1 and end at index 3 or 4: 2 × 2 = 4 slices.
There are no odd numbers at all.
[1], [1, 2], [2, 1] and the last [1]. The full slice has two odd numbers, so it does not count.

hints: Only whether a number is odd matters. Replace each value with 1 if odd and 0 if even. Now you are counting slices whose sum is exactly k.
A window can easily count slices with at most k odd numbers: for each right end, every start from the left edge to the right end works. How do you get exactly k from that?
exactly(k) = atMost(k) − atMost(k − 1). Or keep a prefix count of odd numbers and a hash map of how often each prefix count has appeared.

explain.intuition:
A sliding window is good at "at most": grow the right edge, shrink the left edge while there are more than k odd numbers, and then every slice that ends at right and starts anywhere in the window is valid, which is right − left + 1 slices. "Exactly k" is not monotone in the same way: shrinking a window with k odds can keep it at k for a while (leading evens), so a single window misses slices.

The fix is subtraction: slices with exactly k odds are those with at most k, minus those with at most k − 1. Another view gives the same answer: if odds is the running count of odd numbers, a slice ending here has exactly k odds when it starts right after a prefix with odds − k. A hash map of prefix counts answers that in O(1), the same idea as counting slices with a target sum.
steps: Write a helper atMost(m): slide right over the array, count odd numbers in the window, and move left forward while the count is above m.
After adjusting left, add right − left + 1 to the helper's total.
pitfalls: Counting only the minimal window for each group of k odds. Evens on either side multiply the count, as in the first example.
Using one window and adding 1 each time the count equals k. It misses slices that start at different evens before the first odd.
Forgetting that the prefix-count map must start with count 0 seen once, for slices starting at index 0.

solutions.title: Try every slice
solutions.idea: Fix a start, extend the end and keep a running count of odd numbers.

solutions.title: Prefix counts in a hash map
solutions.idea: A slice has exactly k odds when the prefix count of odds at its end minus the one before its start equals k.

solutions.title: At most k minus at most k − 1
solutions.idea: A sliding window counts slices with at most m odd numbers. The difference of two such counts is exactly k.

followups: Solve it in one pass with O(1) memory by tracking how many evens precede the first odd in the window.
Count slices with between lo and hi odd numbers, inclusive.
